title: Knowledge check: Handling Pagination, Sorting, and Filtering

questions.prompt: In Handling Pagination, Sorting, and Filtering, which statement best describes Page-based pagination?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Query-string values are untrusted and may be missing, repeated or represented as strings. Validate bounds and allowlist supported sort/filter fields before querying data.
This option describes a different concept and does not define page-based pagination (choice 2).
questions.answer_key: Query-string values are untrusted and may be missing, repeated or represented as strings. Validate bounds and allowlist supported sort/filter fields before querying data.
questions.explanation: Query-string values are untrusted and may be missing, repeated or represented as strings. Validate bounds and allowlist supported sort/filter fields before querying data.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Handling Pagination, Sorting, and Filtering?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Request bodies, parameters, and query strings arrive as untrusted values. Parse only the expected content type, enforce size limits, validate and normalize data, and return consistent client errors before business logic runs.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Request bodies, parameters, and query strings arrive as untrusted values. Parse only the expected content type, enforce size limits, validate and normalize data, and return consistent client errors before business logic runs.
questions.explanation: Request bodies, parameters, and query strings arrive as untrusted values. Parse only the expected content type, enforce size limits, validate and normalize data, and return consistent client errors before business logic runs.

questions.prompt: A change related to Handling Pagination, Sorting, and Filtering appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
